subject: FERPA addendum & data residency feasibility for Harbor County SD
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@harbor-csd.org>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonah Pierce <jonah.pierce@educonsortium.org>
Date: 2026-05-28T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: FERPA addendum & residency question for pilot

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — Harbor County (HCSD) liked the inference latency profile, and the tech team is comfortable from a performance standpoint. Before legal will greenlight a small pilot with student PII, they asked for a few confirmations so we can circulate a FERPA-specific addendum to our purchasing team. Can you confirm the following: 

- Will Redwood sign a FERPA addendum that includes a data processing scope limited to inference requests (no student record storage outside ephemeral KV cache)?
- Can you provide a current subprocessor list (or cert that you have none that process student data) and SOC 2 report?
- Is it possible to ensure HCSD student data is processed and retained only in US regions (no cross-border transfers to EU/APAC) for the pilot?

I've attached the HCSD draft of their standard FERPA addendum for reference (FERPA_Addendum_Draft_HCSD_v1.docx) and a data flow they want acknowledged (HCSD_DataFlow_Map.pdf). Goal is a two-week turnaround if feasible.

Appreciate a quick feasibility note and rough timeline.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
General Counsel, Harbor County School District

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@harbor-csd.org>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FERPA addendum & residency question for pilot

Hi Marta — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Vivek (privacy/compliance) and Grace (solutions) to confirm feasibility. Quick notes from me: 

- Redwood has standard language for education customers; we can sign a FERPA addendum that limits processing to runtime inference (we do not persist student records to persistent storage by default).
- We maintain a current Subprocessor List and SOC 2 Type II report; I can share the redacted copies under NDA.
- Residency: hosted API endpoints are multi-region by default, but we offer Dedicated and Private deployment options to guarantee US-only processing. For a pilot of this size, Dedicated (reserved capacity in US region) is usually the fastest path vs full Private.

Let Vivek/Grace weigh in on any legal/controls nuance and estimated timeline. If acceptable, we can propose: 1) provide Subprocessor List + SOC2 within 3 business days under NDA, 2) propose FERPA addendum redline within 4 business days, 3) confirm Dedicated capacity slot and retention settings within 7 business days.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <mruiz@harbor-csd.org>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FERPA addendum & residency question for pilot

Hi all — quick compliance feasibility note from my side.

1) FERPA addendum: Redwood's standard DPA can be adapted into a FERPA addendum. We treat customers as Controllers; Redwood acts as Processor. The addendum will explicitly state processing scope = inference calls + ephemeral KV cache (TTL configurable, default ephemeral). We should be careful about any language that implies storage of student records beyond cache TTL.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is the current Subprocessor_List_202605.pdf (production subprocessors only). For student data: we do not route telemetry/content to external analytics subprocessors without opt-in; telemetry is stored separately and can be disabled for HCSD pilot.

3) Residency / transfers: For hosted customers, we cannot guarantee US-only processing because control plane and some autoscaling decisions are global. However, two viable paths: 
  - Dedicated (US-only GPU pool + control plane with geo-fencing) — fastest and lowest friction for a short pilot.
  - Private deployment (VPC) — complete residency and network control but longer lead time (4–8 weeks + infra setup).

4) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and the last penetration test report are available for sharing under an NDA. We can also provide our data retention controls and KV TTL configuration notes.

Proposed next steps:
- Laura/Grace: share a redline to the HCSD FERPA draft (we can then produce an internal redline) — target EOD Tue (2026-06-01).
- Laura: provide a formal quote for Dedicated slot (1–2 weeks pricing) so procurement can trigger commit.
- Vivek/Karthik: prepare the limited-scope subprocessor attestation and SOC2 package for NDA release (3 business days).

I'll wait for the redline from Laura.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@harbor-csd.org>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-29T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FERPA addendum & residency question for pilot

Marta — attaching our suggested redline to your FERPA draft ("FERPA_Addendum_Redline_Redwood_v1.docx") and a short cover note. Key changes we made (summary):

- Clarified scope to runtime inference and ephemeral KV cache (TTL configurable to as low as 30s for the pilot).
- Explicitly excluded analytics telemetry from student data processing unless HCSD opts in.
- Added option clause: if HCSD needs US-only processing for the pilot, we recommend a Dedicated instance; cost estimates are in the HubSpot quote (link below).
- Standard subprocessors attached; we commit to 30 days notice for changes and to provide expedited subprocessors attestations.

Cover note included in the attachment outlines items that still need negotiation: indemnity caps as related to student data, retention period language, and audit rights.

Attachments: FERPA_Addendum_Redline_Redwood_v1.docx; Subprocessor_List_202605.pdf

Next steps from HCSD: please confirm whether Dedicated is required for the pilot or hosted is acceptable with telemetry disabled. If Dedicated, I will kick off quoting and capacity check.

Best,
Laura

From: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@harbor-csd.org>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonah Pierce <jonah.pierce@educonsortium.org>, Kelly Adams <kelly.adams@lakeside-k12.edu>
Date: 2026-05-31T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FERPA addendum & residency question for pilot

Laura — thank you, and thanks Vivek/Grace for the rapid response. Harbor County is inclined to require US-only processing for this pilot and wants the Dedicated option so we have an auditable, isolated GPU pool. Two quick asks before we proceed: 

1) Please provide the Dedicated slot quote and expected start date (we will need to run procurement).
2) Can you confirm the KV TTL floor (we see 30s noted — confirm that is configurable and enforced for the Dedicated instance)?

If both are doable in the next 3 business days, we'll route the redline to procurement and legal for final review. Looking forward to the SOC2 bundle under NDA.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
General Counsel, Harbor County School District
